Rashi on Shabbat 12b:1:1.hebrew: בתוך חולי ישראל - שמתוך שכוללן עם האחרים, תפלתו נשמעת בזכותן של רבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:1:1.english: Among the sick of Israel - For since he includes him with the others, his prayer is heard through the merit of the many.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:1:2.english: Shevna of Jerusalem - There was a great man in Jerusalem, and his name was Shevna.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:1:3.english: His compassion - [The compassion] of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is abundant.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:1:4.english: Rest [on Shabbat] in peace - Rest on your Sabbath in peace.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:2:1.english: With difficulty they permitted [it] - Because one is distressed.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:2:3.hebrew: זימנין אמר לה - בלשון קדש, וזימנין אמר לה בלשון ארמי. והא לאו לענין שבת נקט:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:2:3.english: Sometimes he said it - In the Holy Tongue, and sometimes he said it in the Aramaic tongue. And this was not cited with regard to the matter of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:2:4.english: For the Divine Presence is with him - And the one praying does not need the ministering angels to attend to him to bring his prayer inside the [celestial] curtain.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:3:1.hebrew: סועד - סומך בתשות כחו. ומשום רבינו יעקב: סוער תרגומו של פוקד, כלומר מבקר, כמו "ואת אחיך תפקוד לשלום" (שמואל א י״ז:י״ח), ומתרגמי' "ואת אחיך תסער לשלם". ולהך לישנא גרסינן: אל תקרי יסעדנו אלא יסערנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:3:1.english: Supports - He supports [him] in his weakness. And in the name of Rabbeinu Yaakov [it was explained]: So'er is the [Aramaic] translation of poked, that is to say, visiting [the sick], as in: "And visit your brothers for [their] welfare" (I Samuel 17:18), and we translate: "And visit your brothers for [their] welfare." And according to this version, we read: Do not read "yis'adenu" [He will support him], but rather "yis'arenu" [He will visit him].

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:3:2.hebrew: מתעטף - מאימת שכינה, כאדם היושב באימה ואין פונה לצדדין:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:3:2.english: [He] wraps himself - Out of awe of the Divine Presence, like a person who sits in awe and does not turn to the sides.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:1.hebrew: ואפי' גבוה - דליכא למיחש להטייה, דכיון דגזור, לא פלוג למילתייהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:1.english: And even [if it is] high - Where there is no concern of tilting [the lamp], for once they decreed, they did not make distinctions in their decree.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:2.hebrew: הא תרי שפיר דמי - שאם יבא להטות, יזכירנו חברו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:2.english: Whereas [for] two it is fine - For if he comes to tilt [the lamp], his fellow will remind him.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:3.hebrew: בשני ענינים - בשתי פרשיות. הואיל וכל אחד מעיין לעצמו, אין מכיר במעשה חבירו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:3.english: In two matters - In two [different] sections. Since each one is studying on his own, he does not notice the actions of his fellow.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:4.hebrew: במדורה - מדורת אש גדולה — אסור, דהואיל ויושבין רחוק זה מזה, ועוד שזנבות האודים סמוכים להם, אין זה מכיר בבא חבירו להבעיר ולחתות:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:4:4.english: By a bonfire - [In the case of] a large bonfire, it is forbidden [to read], since they sit far from one another, and furthermore, the ends of the firebrands are close to them, [so] one does not notice when his fellow comes to kindle and rake [the coals].

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:5:1.hebrew: מותר - לקרות לאור הנר, שאינו רגיל להטות נר בחול מפני חשיבותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:5:1.english: [It is] permitted - To read by the light of the lamp, for he is not accustomed to tilt a lamp on a weekday due to his importance.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:6:1.hebrew: שמש קבוע - לא יבדוק, מפני שאימת רבו עליו אם ימצא בהן דבר מגונה, ובודקן יפה, וחיישינן להטיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:6:1.english: A regular servant - He may not inspect [them], because the fear of his master is upon him if an unseemly thing should be found in them, and he inspects them thoroughly, and we are concerned about [his] tilting [the lamp].

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:6:2.english: [A servant] who is not regular - [The fear of his master] is not cast upon him so much.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:6:3.english: Both this and that [refer] to a regular servant - This is our reading.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:6:4.hebrew: בדנפטא - שהוא מסריח, מותר לבדוק לאורו, דלא אתי להטות:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:6:4.english: With naphtha - Since it is foul-smelling, it is permitted to examine by its light, as he will not come to tilt [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:1.hebrew: שמש שאינו קבוע בדמשחא מאי - כיון שאינו קבוע, אינו מטה אפילו בחול, והלכך בשבת מותר — או דילמא בדמשחא, הואיל ולא מאיס, דרכו להטות בחול הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:1.english: A servant who is not regularly employed with [a lamp of] oil, what is [the ruling]? - Since he is not regularly employed, he does not tilt [the lamp] even on a weekday, and therefore on Shabbat [it is] permitted — or perhaps, with [a lamp of] oil, since it is not repulsive, it is his practice to tilt [it] on a weekday [and it is therefore prohibited]?

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:2.english: The halakha - That it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:3.english: And we do not instruct so - So that they do not treat [the prohibition] lightly.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:4.hebrew: קם שמעי' - דר' ירמיה, דהוא שמש שאינו קבוע בבית רב אסי:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:4.english: His servant stood - [The servant] of Rabbi Yirmeyah, for he was a servant who was not regular in the house of Rav Asi.

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:5.hebrew: אמרה ליה דביתהו - דרב אסי לרב אסי: מר לא עביד הכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:5.english: His wife said to him - [The wife] of Rav Asi [said] to Rav Asi: "The Master does not do so."

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:7:6.english: In accordance with his master - Rabbi Yirmeya, who said: "The halakha is [that it is permitted], and we instruct accordingly."

Rashi on Shabbat 12b:8:1.hebrew: ראשי פרשיות - ומריצן בפיו, שמתוך שראש הפרשה שגורה בפיו, הוא נזכר בכולה למחר, ומסייע את שבעה הקורין בנקודה וטעמיה בלחש:
Rashi on Shabbat 12b:8:1.english: The beginnings of the sections - And he runs them through in his mouth, for since the beginning of the section is fluent in his mouth, he will remember all of it tomorrow and assist the seven readers with the vocalization and its cantillation in a whisper.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:1:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר המקום ירחם עליך כו' - ק' לר"ת: מה מועלת תפלה לר' מאיר ור' יהודה? דקאמר בפ"ק דר"ה (ד' טז. ושם): הכל נידונים בר"ה, וגזר דין שלהם נחתם ביוה"כ — דברי ר"מ. ר' יהודה אומר: הכל נידונין בר"ה, וגזר דין של כל אחד ואחד נחתם בזמנו: בפסח על התבואה, ואדם ביום הכפורים. ר' יוסי אומר: אדם נידון בכל יום. ואמר התם: אמר רב יוסף: כמאן מצלינן האידנא אקצירי ואמריעי? כר' יוסי — משמע דלר"מ ולר' יהודה לא מהניא צלותא! וי"ל, דהכא בשבת שבין ר"ה ובין יוה"כ איירי. ולפי מאי דמשני התם: "איבעית אימא כדר' יצחק, דאמר ר' יצחק: יפה צעקה לאדם בין קודם גז"ד כו'" — אתי הכא שפיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:1:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: "May the Omnipresent have compassion upon you," etc. - Rabbeinu Tam raises a difficulty: How does prayer help according to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda? For it is stated in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (16a and ibid.): "All are judged on Rosh Hashanah, and their sentence is sealed on Yom Kippur" — [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: "All are judged on Rosh Hashanah, and the sentence of each and every one is sealed at its [appointed] time: on Passover concerning grain, and mankind on Yom Kippur." Rabbi Yosei says: "Mankind is judged every day." And [the Gemara] says there: Rav Yosef said: "In accordance with whose [opinion] do we pray nowadays for the sick and for the afflicted? In accordance with Rabbi Yosei" — which implies that according to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda, prayer does not help! And it can be answered that here [in the Baraita in Shabbat], it is dealing with a Shabbat that falls between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. And according to what [the Gemara] answers there: "If you wish, say [it is] in accordance with Rabbi Yitzḥak, as Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Crying out is beneficial for a person both before the sentence [and after the sentence, etc.]," it works out well here.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:1:2.hebrew: שבנא איש ירושלים - ר"ת לא גריס שבנא, דשבנא רשע הוה, ולא מסקינן בשמיה, ד"שם רשעים ירקב", כדאמר בפרק אמר להם הממונה (יומא דף לח:). אלא גרס שכנא, דהוי נמי שם אדם, כדאמר בסוטה (דף כא.): "אלא כשכנא אחי הלל". ונראה לר"י דשפיר גרס שבנא, דאטו אם אחד רשע ושמו אברהם, לא נקרא בשם זה אחר?! ואשכחן דתרי שבנא הוו, כמו שמוכיח בישעיה (כב): דכתיב "שבנא אשר על הבית", וכתיב "וקראתי לעבדי לאליקים וגו' וממשלתך אתן בידו", וכתיב בתר הכי (שם לו): "ויבא אליו אליקים אשר על הבית ושבנא הסופר" — משמע דשבנא אשר על הבית כבר מת, והיה אליקים במקומו, ושבנא הסופר היה אחר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:1:2.english: "Shevna of Jerusalem" - Rabbeinu Tam did not read "Shevna," because Shevna was a wicked man, and we do not name [people] after him, for "the name of the wicked shall rot" (Proverbs 10:7), as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] "Amar Lahem HaMemuneh" (Yoma 38b). Rather, he read "Shekhna," which is also a person's name, as [the Gemara] says in Sotah (21a): "Rather, like Shekhna, the brother of Hillel." And it appears to the Ri that the reading "Shevna" is correct, for is it so that if one [individual] was wicked and his name was Abraham, another person could not be called by this name?! And we find that there were two [men named] Shevna, as is proved in Isaiah (ch. 22): for it is written, "Shevna, who is over the house" (Isaiah 22:15), and it is written, "And I will call My servant Eliakim... and I will commit your authority into his hand" (ibid. 22:20–21), and it is written after that (ibid. 36): "And Eliakim, who was over the house, and Shevna the scribe came to him" — which implies that Shevna who was over the house had already died, and Eliakim was in his place, and Shevna the scribe was another [person].

Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:2:1.hebrew: שאין מלאכי השרת מכירין בלשון ארמי - לבד מגבריאל, כדאמר בסוטה בריש אלו נאמרין (סוטה דף לג.): דאמר מר, בא גבריאל ולמדו שבעים לשונות ליוסף. ותימה, דאפי' מחשבה שבלב כל אדם יודעים, ולשון ארמי אין יודעים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:2:1.english: "For the ministering angels are not familiar with the Aramaic language" - Except for Gabriel, as [the Gemara] says in Sotah at the beginning of [the chapter] "Elu Neemarin" (Sotah 33a): For the Master said, Gabriel came and taught Joseph seventy languages. And it is astonishing: for they know even the thought in the heart of every person, yet they do not know the Aramaic language?!

Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:3:1.hebrew: לא ישב על גבי מטה ולא על ספסל - נראה דדוקא כשחולה שוכב בנמוך, שלא ישב גבוה ממראשותיו של חולה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:3:1.english: "One should sit neither on a bed nor on a bench" - It appears that [this applies] specifically when the sick person is lying low down, so that [the visitor] should not sit higher than the head of the sick person.

Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:5:1.hebrew: רבי נתן אומר קרא והטה - הכא, ובמכות (דף ר:) גבי יהודה בן טבאי שהרג עד זומם, ובהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צו:) גבי הא שנקרע ס"ת בחמתן — לא פריך: "ומה בהמתן של צדיקים אין הקב"ה מביא תקלה כו'"? אומר ר"ת: דלא פריך בשום מקום אלא גבי אכילת איסור, שגנאי הוא לצדיק ביותר. וההוא דערבי פסחים (כסחים דף קג: ושם), דר' ירמיה אישתלי וטעים קודם הבדלה, והנהו דמס' ר"ה (דף כא.), דקאמר "בסים תבשילא דבבלאי בצומא רבה דמערבא" — התם לא הוה מאכל איסור, אלא השעה אסורה. ובבראשית רבה אמרינן: ר' ירמיה שלח לר' זירא חד טרסקל דתאנים, ומסיק: "בין דין לדין מתאכל תאנתא בטבלא" — הא קאמר עלה ר' אבא בר זימנא בשם ר' אליעזר זעירא: "אם הראשונים מלאכים אנו בני אינש, ואם הם בני אינש אנו כחמורים, ולא כחמורו של ר' פנחס בן יאיר":
Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:5:1.english: Rabbi Natan says: He read and tilted [the lamp] - Here, and in Makkot (5b) regarding Yehuda ben Tabbai who executed a [single] plotting witness (eid zomem), and in [the chapter] HaIsha Rabbah (Yevamot 96b) regarding that [incident] where a Torah scroll was torn in their anger — [the Gemara] does not object: "If even through the animals of the righteous the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not bring about a mishap, etc. [all the more so through the righteous themselves]?" Rabbeinu Tam explains that [the Gemara] only raises this objection regarding the consumption of forbidden food, because it is exceedingly disgraceful for a righteous person [to ingest something forbidden]. And as for that [incident] in [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 106b), where Rabbi Yirmiyah forgot and tasted [food] before Havdalah, and those [cases] in Tractate Rosh Hashanah (21a), where it is said, "How tasty is the dish of the Babylonians on the Great Fast of the West [the Land of Israel]!" — there, it was not forbidden food [in itself], but rather the time [of eating] that was forbidden. And [as for that which] we say in Bereishit Rabbah: Rabbi Yirmiyah sent Rabbi Zeira a basket of figs, and [the Midrash] concludes, "Between this one and that one, a fig was eaten while untithed (tevel)" — behold, Rabbi Abba bar Zimna said regarding this in the name of Rabbi Eliezer Ze'eira: "If the earlier [generations] were angels, we are human beings; and if they were human beings, we are like donkeys — and not like the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair!"

Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:7:1.hebrew: שמש שאינו קבוע בדמשחא מאי - ללישנא בתרא מבעי ליה. ור"ת גריס: "הא והא בשמש שאינו קבוע; איבעיא להו: שמש קבוע בדמשחא מאי?" — דשמש שאינו קבוע בודק יפה שלא יעבירוהו, אבל קבוע לא מרתת שיעבירוהו בשביל כך, כיון שהוקבע כבר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 12b:7:1.english: "[Regarding] a servant who is not regularly employed with [an] oil [lamp], what is [the ruling]?" - This [dilemma] is needed according to the latter version [of the resolution]. And Rabbeinu Tam reads: "Both this and that [baraita speak] of a servant who is not regularly employed; a dilemma was raised before them: [Regarding] a regularly employed servant with [an] oil [lamp], what is [the ruling]?" — for a servant who is not regularly employed examines [the dishes] meticulously so that they will not dismiss him, but a regularly employed servant is not afraid that they will dismiss him on account of this, since he has already been permanently established.
